title.zh: 卷三十六 義兒傳第二十四: 李嗣昭 李嗣本 李嗣恩 李存信 李存孝 李存進 李存璋 李存賢
title.en: Volume 36 Biographies of Righteous Sons 16: Li Sizhao, Li Siben, Li Si'en, Li Cunxin, Li Cunxiao, Li Cunjin, Li Cunzhang, Li Cunxian
title.raw: 卷三十六 義兒傳第二十四: 李嗣昭 李嗣本 李嗣恩 李存信 李存孝 李存進 李存璋 李存賢 Volume 36 Biographies of Righteous Sons 16: Li Sizhao, Li Siben, Li Si'en, Li Cunxin, Li Cunxiao, Li Cunjin, Li Cunzhang, Li Cunxian

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 世道衰，人倫壞，而親疏之理反其常，干戈起於骨肉，異類合為父子。

translations.literal: As the age decays and human bonds corrupt, the logic of kin and stranger is reversed; arms rise among flesh and blood, and unrelated kinds are joined as father and son.
translations.idiomatic: The age rots, human bonds snap, and near and far trade places—kin turn on kin, strangers are made fathers and sons.

sentences.zh: 開平、顯德五十年間，天下五代而實八姓，其三出於丐養。

translations.literal: In the fifty years from Kaiping to Xiande, the realm saw five dynasties but eight ruling surnames in truth—three of them came from beggar-adoption.
translations.idiomatic: From Kaiping to Xiande, fifty years saw five dynasties on paper and eight ruling houses in fact—three born of beggar-adoption.

sentences.zh: 蓋其大者取天下，其次立功名、位將相，豈非因時之隙，以利合而相資者邪！

translations.literal: The greatest seized the realm; the next won merit and stood as generals and chancellors—is this not men who, through gaps in the times, joined by profit to aid one another?
translations.idiomatic: Some took the realm; others won fame as generals and chancellors—did they not seize the moment, unite on profit, and lift each other up?

sentences.zh: 唐自號沙陀，起代北，其所與俱皆一時雄傑虣武之士，往往養以為兒，號「義兒軍」，至其有天下，多用以成功業，及其亡也亦由焉。

translations.literal: Tang styled itself Shatuo, rising from north of Dai; all who marched with it were fierce heroes of the age—and often they were raised as sons, called the "Adopted Sons Army." When Tang had the realm, many were used to complete the work; when it perished, that was likewise the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Tang called itself Shatuo, rose beyond Dai, and marched with the fiercest warriors of the age—often adopted as sons in the "Adopted Sons Army." They built the realm; they also undid it.

sentences.zh: 太祖養子多矣，其可紀者九人，其一是為明宗，其次曰嗣昭、嗣本、嗣恩、存信、存孝、存進、存璋、存賢。

translations.literal: Taizu adopted many sons; nine are worth recording—one became Mingzong; the rest were called Sizhao, Siben, Si'en, Cunxin, Cunxiao, Cunjin, Cunzhang, and Cunxian.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took many adopted sons; nine merit record—one became Mingzong; the others: Sizhao, Siben, Si'en, Cunxin, Cunxiao, Cunjin, Cunzhang, Cunxian.

sentences.zh: 作《義兒傳》。

translations.literal: [The author] composed "The Biography of Adopted Sons."
translations.idiomatic: Hence this "Biography of Adopted Sons."

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭

translations.literal: Li Sizhao
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭，本姓韓氏，汾州太谷縣民家子也。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao—originally surnamed Han, a commoner's son of Taigu County in Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao was born Han, a farmer's son in Taigu County, Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖出獵，至其家，見其林中郁郁有氣，甚異之，召其父問焉。

translations.literal: Taizu went out hunting, came to his home, saw a lush aura in the woods and found it very strange; he summoned the father to ask.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu hunted there, saw an uncanny vigor in the grove, and called the father to question him.

sentences.zh: 父言家適生兒，太祖因遺以金帛而取之，命其弟克柔養以為子。

translations.literal: The father said a son had just been born at home; Taizu therefore left gold and silks and took the boy, ordering his younger brother Kerou to raise him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: The father said a son had just been born; Taizu left gold and silks, took the infant, and had his brother Kerou raise him as a son.

sentences.zh: 初名進通，後更名嗣昭。

translations.literal: At first named Jintong; later renamed Sizhao.
translations.idiomatic: First named Jintong; later Sizhao.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭為人短小，而膽勇過人。

translations.literal: Sizhao was short in stature, yet his courage surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao was small in frame but bolder than any man around him.

sentences.zh: 初喜嗜酒，太祖嘗微戒之，遂終身不飲。

translations.literal: At first he loved wine; Taizu once gently warned him, and he never drank again for life.
translations.idiomatic: He had loved wine until Taizu gently reproved him—then he never drank again.

sentences.zh: 太祖愛其謹厚，常從用兵，為衙內指揮使。

translations.literal: Taizu loved his prudence and steadiness, kept him on campaigns, and made him commander of the inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu prized his steady character, kept him in the field, and made him commander of the inner guard.

sentences.zh: 天復元年，梁破河中，執王珂，取晉、絳、慈、隰，因大舉擊晉，圍太原。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianfu, Liang broke Hezhong, seized Wang Ke, took Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi, and then launched a great assault on Jin, besieging Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu's first year Liang took Hezhong and Wang Ke, seized Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi, and marched in force on Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭日以精騎出擊梁兵，會大雨，梁軍解去。

translations.literal: Sizhao daily led picked cavalry out to strike Liang; a great rain fell and the Liang army lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day Sizhao led elite horsemen against Liang; heavy rain came and Liang broke camp.

sentences.zh: 晉汾州刺史李瑭叛降梁軍，梁軍已去，嗣昭復取汾州，斬瑭。

translations.literal: Jin's Fenzhou prefect Li Tang rebelled and surrendered to Liang; after Liang had gone, Sizhao retook Fenzhou and beheaded Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Fenzhou prefect Li Tang defected to Liang; when Liang withdrew, Sizhao retook the city and executed Tang.

sentences.zh: 遂出陰地，取慈州，降其刺史唐禮。

translations.literal: He then marched into Yindi, took Cizhou, and received the surrender of its prefect Tang Li.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed into Yindi, seized Cizhou, and won prefect Tang Li's surrender.

sentences.zh: 又取隰州，降其刺史張瑰。

translations.literal: He also took Xizhou and received the surrender of its prefect Zhang Gui.
translations.idiomatic: He took Xizhou as well; prefect Zhang Gui submitted.

sentences.zh: 是歲，梁軍西犯京師，圍鳳翔，嗣昭乘間攻梁晉、絳，戰平陽，執梁將一人。

translations.literal: That year Liang invaded the western capital and besieged Fengxiang; Sizhao seized the interval to attack Liang in Jin and Jiang, fought at Pingyang, and captured one Liang general.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liang struck west and besieged Fengxiang; Sizhao struck Liang in Jin and Jiang, fought at Pingyang, and took a Liang general.

sentences.zh: 進攻蒲縣。

translations.literal: He advanced and attacked Pu County.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to attack Pu County.

sentences.zh: 梁朱友寧、氏叔琮以兵十萬迎擊之，嗣昭等敗走，友寧追之，晉遣李存信率兵迎嗣昭，存信又敗。

translations.literal: Liang's Zhu Youning and Shi Shuzong met him with a hundred thousand men; Sizhao and the rest were beaten and fled; Youning pursued; Jin sent Li Cunxin with troops to meet Sizhao, and Cunxin was beaten too.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youning and Shi Shuzong brought a hundred thousand men; Sizhao was routed; Youning pursued; Jin sent Li Cunxin to rescue him—and Cunxin lost as well.

sentences.zh: 梁軍遂圍太原，而慈、隰、汾州復入於梁。

translations.literal: The Liang army then besieged Taiyuan, and Ci, Xi, and Fenzhou again fell to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang besieged Taiyuan again; Ci, Xi, and Fen returned to Liang.

sentences.zh: 太祖大恐，謀走雲州，李存信等勸太祖奔於契丹，嗣昭力爭以為不可，賴劉太妃亦言之，乃止。

translations.literal: Taizu was greatly afraid and planned flight to Yunzhou; Li Cunxin and others urged him to flee to the Khitan; Sizhao argued fiercely that this must not be done; thanks also to Consort Liu speaking likewise, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu panicked and planned escape to Yunzhou; Cunxin urged flight to the Khitan; Sizhao and Consort Liu protested until he stayed.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭晝夜出奇兵擊梁軍，梁軍解去，嗣昭復取汾、慈、隰。

translations.literal: Sizhao day and night sent surprise forces against Liang; Liang lifted the siege; Sizhao retook Fen, Ci, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao harried Liang day and night with ambushes until they withdrew; then he retook Fen, Ci, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，鎮、定皆已絕晉而附梁。

translations.literal: That year Zhen and Ding both broke with Jin and attached to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhen and Ding abandoned Jin for Liang.

sentences.zh: 晉外失大國之援，內亡諸州，仍歲之間，孤城被圍者再。

translations.literal: Jin lost great-power aid abroad and lost its prefectures within; within years its lone city was besieged twice.
translations.idiomatic: Jin lost its great allies abroad and its prefectures within; within years the lone capital was besieged twice.

sentences.zh: 於此時，嗣昭力戰之功為多。

translations.literal: At this time Sizhao's feats in hard fighting were the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In that crisis no one fought harder than Sizhao.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年，與周德威攻梁潞州，降丁會，以嗣昭為昭義軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianyou he joined Zhou Dewei in attacking Liang at Luzhou, received Ding Hui's surrender, and made Sizhao military governor of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou's third year he and Zhou Dewei took Luzhou; Ding Hui surrendered; Sizhao became governor of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 梁遣李思安將兵十萬攻潞，築夾城以圍之。

translations.literal: Liang sent Li Si'an with a hundred thousand men to attack Lu, building twin walled corridors to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Li Si'an with a hundred thousand men, ringed Lu with twin siege walls.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖遣人招降嗣昭，嗣昭斬其使者，閉城拒守，逾年，莊宗始攻破夾城。

translations.literal: Liang's Taizu sent men to summon Sizhao to surrender; Sizhao beheaded the envoys, shut the gates, and held out for more than a year before Zhuangzong finally broke the twin walls.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Taizu sent envoys; Sizhao killed them, barred the gates, and held a year until Zhuangzong broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭完緝兵民，撫養甚有恩意。

translations.literal: Sizhao restored troops and people and ruled them with real kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao rebuilt army and populace and governed them with genuine care.

sentences.zh: 梁、晉戰胡柳，晉軍敗，周德威戰死。

translations.literal: Jin and Liang fought at Willow Hu; Jin was defeated and Zhou Dewei died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Willow Hu Jin lost; Zhou Dewei fell.

sentences.zh: 莊宗懼，欲收兵還臨濮，嗣昭曰：「梁軍已勝，旦暮思歸。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong feared and wished to withdraw to Linpu; Sizhao said: "The Liang army has already won and soon will think of returning home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong feared retreat to Linpu; Sizhao said: "Liang has won—they will soon want to go home.

sentences.zh: 吾若收軍，使彼休息，整而復出，何以當之？

translations.literal: If we withdraw and let them rest, then come out again refreshed—how can we face them?
translations.idiomatic: Pull back now and they will rest, regroup, and strike again—how will we stand against them?

sentences.zh: 宜以精騎撓之，因其勞乏，可以勝也。

translations.literal: We ought to harass them with picked cavalry; while they are weary and spent, we can defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Harass them with elite cavalry while they are exhausted—that is how we win.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗然之。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁軍已登無石山，莊宗遣嗣昭轉擊山北，而自以銀槍軍趨而曰：「今日之戰，得山者勝！

translations.literal: At that time Liang had already climbed Wushi Mountain; Zhuangzong sent Sizhao to strike north of the mountain while he himself led the Silver Spear Army in a rush, crying: "Today's battle—who holds the mountain wins!
translations.idiomatic: Liang had taken Wushi Mountain; Zhuangzong sent Sizhao around the north face while he led the Silver Spear Army shouting: "Who holds the hill today wins!

sentences.zh: 」晉軍皆爭登山，梁軍遽下，陣於山西，晉軍從上急擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: " The Jin army all scrambled up the slope; the Liang army rushed down and formed west of the mountain; the Jin army pressed from above and crushed them.
translations.idiomatic: " Jin soldiers clawed up the slope; Liang rushed down to the west face; Jin struck from above and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 於是晉城德勝矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jin held Desheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jin held Desheng from that day.

sentences.zh: 周德威死，嗣昭權知幽州，居數月，以李紹宏代之。

translations.literal: When Zhou Dewei died, Sizhao acted as provisional governor of Youzhou; after several months Li Shaohong replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: After Dewei's death Sizhao governed Youzhou provisionally; months later Li Shaohong replaced him.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭將去，幽州人皆號哭閉關遮留之，嗣昭夜遁，乃得去。

translations.literal: As Sizhao was about to leave, the people of Youzhou wailed, shut the passes, and blocked him; Sizhao fled by night before he could get away.
translations.idiomatic: When he prepared to leave, Youzhou wept, closed the gates, and tried to keep him; he slipped away by night.

sentences.zh: 十九年，從莊宗擊契丹於望都，莊宗為契丹圍之數十重，嗣昭以三百騎決圍，取莊宗以出。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he followed Zhuangzong against the Khitan at Wangdu; Zhuangzong was ringed dozens of layers deep; Sizhao with three hundred horsemen broke the encirclement and brought Zhuangzong out.
translations.idiomatic: In year nineteen he followed Zhuangzong against the Khitan at Wangdu; Zhuangzong was trapped in rings of enemy lines; Sizhao with three hundred riders cut him free.

sentences.zh: 是時，晉遣閻寶攻張文禮於鎮州，寶為鎮人所敗，乃以嗣昭代之。

translations.literal: At that time Jin sent Yan Bao to attack Zhang Wenli at Zhenzhou; Bao was beaten by the men of Zhen and Sizhao replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had sent Yan Bao against Zhang Wenli at Zhenzhou; Zhen beat Bao, and Sizhao took his place.

sentences.zh: 鎮兵出掠九門，嗣昭以奇兵擊之，鎮軍且盡，餘三人匿破垣中，嗣昭馳馬射之，反為賊射中腦，嗣昭顧箙中矢盡，拔矢於腦，射殺一人，還營而卒。

translations.literal: Zhen troops raided Jiumen; Sizhao ambushed them and nearly wiped them out; three survivors hid in a broken wall; Sizhao galloped up and shot them, but was himself shot in the head by a bandit; Sizhao saw his quiver empty, pulled the arrow from his skull, killed one man, returned to camp, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen raided Jiumen; Sizhao ambushed them and nearly annihilated the force; three hid in ruined walls; he charged to shoot them and took an arrow in the skull; quiver empty, he wrenched the shaft from his head, killed one more, rode back to camp, and died.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭諸子，繼儔長而懦，其弟繼韜囚之以自立，莊宗方與梁兵相持河上，不暇究其事，因即以為昭義軍留後。

translations.literal: Of Sizhao's sons, the eldest Jichou was grown yet timid; his brother Jitao imprisoned him to rule alone; Zhuangzong was then locked with Liang on the Yellow River and had no leisure to investigate, and at once made Jitao acting governor of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao's eldest son Jichou was grown but weak; brother Jitao jailed him and seized power; Zhuangzong, fighting Liang on the river, had no time to inquire and confirmed Jitao as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 繼韜委其政於魏琢、申蒙，琢等常教繼韜反，繼韜未決。

translations.literal: Jitao handed government to Wei Zhuo and Shen Meng; Zhuo and the rest often urged Jitao to rebel, but Jitao had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Jitao left rule to Wei Zhuo and Shen Meng, who kept urging rebellion; he still hesitated.

sentences.zh: 莊宗在魏，以事召監軍張居翰、節度判官任圜。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was at Wei and summoned the army supervisor Zhang Juhang and the prefectural judge Ren Yuan on business.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was at Wei and summoned army supervisor Zhang Juhang and judge Ren Yuan.

sentences.zh: 琢等以謂莊宗召居翰等問繼韜事，繼韜且見誅，因以語趣之，繼韜乃遣其弟繼遠入梁，梁末帝即拜繼韜同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Zhuo and the rest thought Zhuangzong had summoned Juhang and the rest to question the Jitao affair and that Jitao would soon be executed; they therefore pressed him with words, and Jitao sent his brother Jiyuan into Liang; Liang's Last Emperor at once made Jitao co-chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo believed Zhuangzong had called them to judge Jitao's treason and pressed him to act; Jitao sent Jiyuan to Liang, and the Last Emperor made him co-chancellor at once.

sentences.zh: 居數月，莊宗滅梁，繼韜將走契丹，會赦至，乃已，因隨其母朝於京師，繼遠諫曰：「兄為臣子，以反為名，復何面以見天子？

translations.literal: Months later Zhuangzong destroyed Liang; Jitao was about to flee to the Khitan when an amnesty arrived and he stopped; he then followed his mother to court at the capital; Jiyuan remonstrated: "Brother, as a subject you are known for rebellion—what face can you show the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Months later Zhuangzong ended Liang; Jitao nearly fled to the Khitan until amnesty came; he followed his mother to the capital; Jiyuan said: "You rebelled as a subject—what face have you to see the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 且潞城堅而倉廩實，不如閉城坐食積粟，以延歲月，愈於往而就戮也。

translations.literal: And Luzhou's walls are strong and its granaries full—better to shut the gates and live on stored grain to buy time than go and accept execution.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou's walls are strong and its stores full—shut the gates, eat the grain, and buy time rather than walk to your death.

sentences.zh: 」繼韜不聽。

translations.literal: " Jitao would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Jitao would not hear him.

sentences.zh: 繼韜母楊氏，善畜財，平生居積行販，至貲百萬。

translations.literal: Jitao's mother, Lady Yang, was skilled at hoarding wealth; all her life she traded and stored until her assets reached a million.
translations.idiomatic: Jitao's mother Lady Yang hoarded wealth all her life through trade until she held a million in assets.

sentences.zh: 當嗣昭為梁圍以夾城彌年，軍用乏絕，楊氏之積，蓋有助焉。

translations.literal: When Sizhao was besieged by Liang in the twin walls for a year and military supplies ran out, Lady Yang's stores surely helped.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang ringed Sizhao for a year and supplies failed, Lady Yang's hoard kept the army alive.

sentences.zh: 至是，乃賫銀數十萬兩至京師，厚賂宦官、伶人，宦官、伶人皆言：「繼韜初無惡意，為奸人所誤耳。

translations.literal: Now she brought several hundred thousand taels of silver to the capital and bribed eunuchs and actors lavishly; eunuchs and actors all said: "Jitao never meant evil—villains misled him."
translations.idiomatic: She now sent hundreds of thousands of taels of silver to the capital and bribed eunuchs and actors, who all said Jitao had meant no harm—only villains had misled him.

sentences.zh: 」楊夫人亦以賂謁劉皇后，劉皇后為言：「嗣昭功臣，宜蒙恩貸。

translations.literal: Lady Yang also bribed Empress Liu; the empress spoke for her: "Sizhao was a meritorious minister—his house should receive grace and pardon."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang bribed Empress Liu, who pleaded: "Sizhao served with merit—his line deserves mercy."

sentences.zh: 」由是莊宗釋繼韜。

translations.literal: Thereby Zhuangzong released Jitao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong freed Jitao.

sentences.zh: 嘗從獵，寵倖無間。

translations.literal: He once followed the hunt and was favored without interval.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted at court and enjoyed unbroken favor.

sentences.zh: 李存渥尤切齒，數詆責之，繼韜懷不自安，復賂宦官、伶人求歸鎮，莊宗不許。

translations.literal: Li Cunwo especially gnashed his teeth and often reviled him; Jitao lived in unease, bribed eunuchs and actors again to beg return to his command, and Zhuangzong refused.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunwo hated him bitterly and often denounced him; uneasy, Jitao bribed eunuchs and actors to plead for his post back—Zhuangzong refused.

sentences.zh: 繼韜陰使人告繼遠，令起變於軍中，冀天子遣己往安緝之，事泄，斬於天津橋。

translations.literal: Jitao secretly sent word to Jiyuan to raise a mutiny in the army, hoping the Son of Heaven would send him to pacify it; the plot leaked and he was beheaded at Tianjin Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly told Jiyuan to stir mutiny in the army so the throne would send him to calm it; exposed, he was beheaded at Tianjin Bridge.

sentences.zh: 其二子嘗為質於梁，莊宗破梁得之，撫其背曰：「爾幼，猶能佐其父反，長復何為乎？

translations.literal: His two sons had once been hostages in Liang; when Zhuangzong destroyed Liang he recovered them, stroked their backs, and said: "You are young, yet could help your father rebel—what will you do when grown?
translations.idiomatic: Two sons had been Liang hostages; when Zhuangzong took them he stroked their backs and said: "You are children, yet helped your father rebel—what will you do grown?

sentences.zh: 」至是因並誅之。

translations.literal: " Now for this they were executed together.
translations.idiomatic: " Now they were killed with him.

sentences.zh: 即遣人斬繼遠，以繼儔知潞州事。

translations.literal: He at once sent men to behead Jiyuan and put Jichou in charge of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to kill Jiyuan and left Jichou governing Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 已而召繼儔還京師，繼儔悉取繼韜妓妾珍玩，而不時即路。

translations.literal: Soon he summoned Jichou back to the capital; Jichou took all of Jitao's concubines and treasures and would not set out on time.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he recalled Jichou to the capital; Jichou seized Jitao's women and treasures and delayed his departure.

sentences.zh: 其弟繼達怒曰：「吾兄父子誅死，而大兄不仁，利其貲財，淫其妻妾，吾所不忍也！

translations.literal: His brother Jida raged: "My brother and his son were executed, yet the eldest is heartless—profiting from his wealth and violating his wives and concubines—I cannot bear it!
translations.idiomatic: Brother Jida raged: "Father and son were slaughtered, yet the eldest steals his wealth and takes his women—I will not endure it!

sentences.zh: 」乃服缞麻，引數百騎坐戟門，使人入殺繼儔。

translations.literal: He put on mourning dress, led several hundred horsemen to sit at the Halberd Gate, and sent men in to kill Jichou.
translations.idiomatic: He donned mourning, seated several hundred riders at the Halberd Gate, and sent men to kill Jichou.

sentences.zh: 節度副使李繼珂募市人千餘攻繼達，繼達走城外，自剄死。

translations.literal: Vice-governor Li Jike recruited more than a thousand townsmen to attack Jida; Jida fled outside the walls and cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Vice-governor Li Jike raised a thousand townsfolk against Jida; Jida fled beyond the wall and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭七子，至明宗時，子繼能坐笞殺其母主藏婢，婢家告變，言繼能反，與其弟繼襲皆見殺，惟一子繼忠僅免。

translations.literal: Of Sizhao's seven sons, by Mingzong's time son Jineng was executed for beating to death his mother's stewardess; the maid's family reported a mutiny, saying Jineng had rebelled, and he and his brother Jixi were both killed—only one son, Jizhong, barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Of Sizhao's seven sons, under Mingzong Jineng was killed for flogging his mother's stewardess to death; her kin cried rebellion, and he and Jixi died—only Jizhong survived.

sentences.zh: 繼忠家於晉陽，楊氏所積餘貲猶巨萬，晉高祖自太原起兵，召契丹為援，契丹求賂，高祖貸於繼忠以取足。

translations.literal: Jizhong lived at Jinyang; Lady Yang's remaining hoard still ran to tens of thousands; when Jin Gaozu raised his army from Taiyuan and called the Khitan as ally, the Khitan demanded bribes and Gaozu borrowed from Jizhong to make up the sum.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhong lived at Jinyang on Lady Yang's remaining fortune of tens of thousands; when Jin Gaozu marched from Taiyuan with Khitan aid, he borrowed from Jizhong to pay the Khitan bribe.

sentences.zh: 高祖入立，甚德之，以為沂、棣、單三州刺史，開運中卒。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he was deeply grateful and made him prefect of Yi, Di, and Shan; he died in the Kaiyun era.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu rewarded him with the prefectures of Yi, Di, and Shan; he died in the Kaiyun years.

sentences.zh: 楊氏平生積產，嗣昭父子三人賴之。

translations.literal: Lady Yang's lifetime accumulation—Sizhao and his three sons all relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang's lifetime hoard sustained Sizhao and three generations of sons.

sentences.zh: 嗣本，本姓張氏，雁門人也。

translations.literal: Siben—originally surnamed Zhang, a man of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siben was born Zhang, from Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 世為銅冶鎮將。

translations.literal: His family for generations were commandants of Tongye.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had long held Tongye as hereditary commandants.

sentences.zh: 嗣本少事太祖，太祖愛之，賜以姓名，養為子。

translations.literal: Siben in youth served Taizu; Taizu loved him, granted him the surname and personal name, and raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: He served Taizu young; Taizu favored him, gave him the Li surname and a new name, and adopted him.

sentences.zh: 從擊居庸關，以功遷義兒軍使。

translations.literal: He followed the assault on Juyong Pass and was promoted for merit to commander of the Adopted Sons Army.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Juyong Pass and rose to command the Adopted Sons Army.

sentences.zh: 從破王行瑜，遷威遠軍使。

translations.literal: He followed the defeat of Wang Xingyu and was made commander of the Weiyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He helped crush Wang Xingyu and became commander of the Weiyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 從攻羅弘信，以先鋒兵破湯陰。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Luo Hongxin and with vanguard troops broke Tangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Luo Hongxin and broke Tangyin at the van.

sentences.zh: 從莊宗破潞州夾城。

translations.literal: He followed Zhuangzong in breaking Liang's twin walls at Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhuangzong when Luzhou's twin siege walls fell.

sentences.zh: 累以戰功遷代州刺史、雲州防禦使、振武節度使，號威信可汗。

translations.literal: By repeated battle honors he rose to prefect of Dai, defender of Yun, and military governor of Zhenwu, styled the Trustworthy Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Battle after battle raised him to prefect of Dai, defender of Yun, and governor of Zhenwu, titled Trustworthy Khan.

sentences.zh: 天祐十三年，從莊宗擊劉鄩於故元城，下洺、磁諸州，六月，還軍振武。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianyou he followed Zhuangzong against Liu Yun at Old Yuancheng, took Bo and Ci prefectures, and in the sixth month returned his army to Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou's thirteenth year he followed Zhuangzong against Liu Yun at Old Yuancheng, took Bo and Ci, and in the sixth month marched back to Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 契丹入代北，攻蔚州，嗣本戰歿。

translations.literal: The Khitan entered north of Dai and attacked Weizhou; Siben died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded north of Dai and struck Weizhou, Siben fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 嗣恩，本姓駱，吐谷渾部人也。

translations.literal: Si'en—originally surnamed Luo, of the Tuyuhun tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Li Si'en was born Luo, of the Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 少事太祖，能騎射，為鐵林軍將，稍以戰功遷突陣指揮使，賜姓名，以為子。

translations.literal: In youth he served Taizu, could ride and shoot, was a Iron Forest general, and by degrees rose through battle honors to commander of the Shock Array, was granted the surname and personal name, and was taken as a son.
translations.idiomatic: He served Taizu young, excelled at horse and bow, rose through the Iron Forest and Shock Array commands, received the Li name, and was adopted.

sentences.zh: 從敗康懷英於河西，遷左廂馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed the defeat of Kang Huaiying west of the river and was made commander of the left wing horse army.
translations.idiomatic: He helped defeat Kang Huaiying west of the river and commanded the left wing horse army.

sentences.zh: 從李嗣昭援朱友謙於河中，與梁兵力戰，槊中其口，戰不已。

translations.literal: He followed Li Sizhao to relieve Zhu Youqian at Hezhong, fought Liang with great force, took a spear through the mouth, and did not cease fighting.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Sizhao to relieve Zhu Youqian at Hezhong, fought Liang head-on, took a spear through the mouth, and kept fighting.

sentences.zh: 遷遼州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Liao.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Liao.

sentences.zh: 從莊宗入魏，遷天雄軍馬步都指揮使。

translations.literal: He followed Zhuangzong into Wei and was made commander of all horse and foot of the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Wei with Zhuangzong and commanded all horse and foot of Tianxiong.

sentences.zh: 劉鄩攻太原，兵趣樂平，嗣恩從後追之，自佗道先入太原以守。

translations.literal: Liu Yun attacked Taiyuan and his troops pressed toward Leping; Si'en followed from behind, took another road first into Taiyuan to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yun marched on Taiyuan toward Leping, Si'en trailed behind, cut by another road, and entered Taiyuan first to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 鄩兵去，嗣恩亦以兵會莊宗於魏，從戰於莘。

translations.literal: When Yun's troops left, Si'en also brought troops to join Zhuangzong at Wei and fought at Xin.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun withdrew, Si'en joined Zhuangzong at Wei and fought at Xin.

sentences.zh: 遷代州刺史、石嶺關已北都知兵馬使、振武節度使。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Dai, commander of all forces north of Shiling Pass, and military governor of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: He became prefect of Dai, commander north of Shiling Pass, and governor of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 天祐十五年，卒於太原。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianyou he died at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou's fifteenth year he died at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 追贈太尉。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 存信，本姓張氏，其父君政，回鶻李思忠之部人也。

translations.literal: Cunxin—originally surnamed Zhang; his father Junzheng was of the tribe of Huihe Li Sizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxin was born Zhang; his father Junzheng came from the tribe of Uyghur Li Sizhong.

sentences.zh: 存信少善騎射，能四夷語，通六蕃書。

translations.literal: Cunxin in youth excelled at riding and shooting, knew the languages of the four barbarians, and mastered the scripts of the six frontier peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Young Cunxin mastered horse and bow, spoke the tongues of the border peoples, and read their six scripts.

sentences.zh: 從太祖起代北，入關破黃巢，累以功為馬步軍都指揮使，遂賜姓名，以為子。

translations.literal: He followed Taizu in rising north of Dai, entered the passes and broke Huang Chao, and by repeated honors became commander of all horse and foot, was granted the surname and personal name, and was taken as a son.
translations.idiomatic: He rose with Taizu beyond Dai, entered the passes against Huang Chao, rose to command all horse and foot, received the Li name, and was adopted.

sentences.zh: 存信與存孝俱為養子，材勇不及存孝，而存信不為之下，由是交惡，存孝所為，存信每沮激之，存孝卒得罪死。

translations.literal: Cunxin and Cunxiao were both adopted sons; in talent and courage he did not match Cunxiao, yet Cunxin would not yield; hence they became enemies; whatever Cunxiao did, Cunxin always thwarted and provoked him, and Cunxiao in the end offended and died.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin and Cunxiao were both adopted sons; Cunxin lacked Cunxiao's brilliance yet refused to bow—so they hated each other; Cunxin blocked and baited him until Cunxiao offended and died.

sentences.zh: 而存信數從征伐，以功領郴州刺史。

translations.literal: Yet Cunxin followed many campaigns and by merit held the prefecture of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Still, Cunxin campaigned repeatedly and won Chen prefecture by merit.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣將兵救朱宣，存信屯於莘縣，為羅弘信所擊，存信敗，亡太祖子落落。

translations.literal: Taizu sent him with troops to rescue Zhu Xuan; Cunxin encamped at Xin County, was struck by Luo Hongxin, was defeated, and lost Taizu's son Luo Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent him to rescue Zhu Xuan; he camped at Xin County, was smashed by Luo Hongxin, and lost Taizu's son Luo Luo.

sentences.zh: 後從太祖討劉仁恭，大敗於安塞。

translations.literal: Later he followed Taizu in punishing Liu Rengong and was greatly defeated at Anse.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Taizu against Liu Rengong and suffered a crushing defeat at Anse.

sentences.zh: 太祖大怒，顧存信曰：「昨日吾醉，公不能為我戰邪？

translations.literal: Taizu flew into a great rage, turned to Cunxin, and said: “Yesterday I was drunk—could you not fight for me?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu erupted in fury and turned on Cunxin: “Yesterday I was drunk—why would you not fight for me?

sentences.zh: 古人三敗，公已二矣。

translations.literal: The ancients spoke of three defeats—you already have two.”
translations.idiomatic: The ancients allowed three defeats—you already have two.”

sentences.zh: 」將殺之，存信叩頭謝罪而免。

translations.literal: He was about to kill him; Cunxin kowtowed in confession and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to execute him, but Cunxin kowtowed until the sentence was lifted.

sentences.zh: 由是大懼，常稱疾，天復二年卒，年四十一。

translations.literal: From then on he lived in great fear and often claimed illness; in the second year of Tianfu he died, aged forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: After that he lived in dread and often pleaded sickness; in Tianfu 2 (902) he died at forty-one.

sentences.zh: 明年，潞州軍亂，殺李克恭以歸唐，梁遣李讜攻李罕之於澤州，存孝以騎兵五千救之。

translations.literal: The next year the Lu Prefecture army mutinied, killed Li Ke Gong, and submitted to Tang; Liang sent Li Chan to attack Li Hanzhi at Ze Prefecture, and Cunxiao led five thousand cavalry to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Lu Prefecture mutinied, killed Li Ke Gong, and returned to Tang; Liang sent Li Chan against Li Hanzhi at Zezhou, and Cunxiao rode in with five thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 梁軍呼罕之曰：「公常恃太原以為命，今上黨已歸唐，唐兵大集，圍太原，沙陀將無穴以自處，公復誰恃而不降乎？

translations.literal: The Liang army called to Hanzhi: “You always relied on Taiyuan for your life; now Shangdang has returned to Tang, Tang troops mass at the gates, Taiyuan is besieged, and the Shatuo generals have no hole to hide in—on whom will you rely if you do not surrender?”
translations.idiomatic: Liang shouted to Hanzhi: “Taiyuan was your lifeline—Shangdang is Tang again, Tang armies gather, Taiyuan is ringed, and the Shatuo have nowhere to burrow. Who is left for you if you will not yield?”

sentences.zh: 」存孝以精騎五百繞梁柵而呼曰：「我沙陀之求穴者，待爾肉以食軍，可令肥者出鬥！

translations.literal: Cunxiao with five hundred elite horse circled the Liang stockade and called: “I am the Shatuo hole-seeker—your flesh will feed my army! Send out your fat men to fight!”
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao swept five hundred picked riders around the Liang camp and yelled: “I am the Shatuo with nowhere left to hide—I mean to eat your flesh to feed my men! Let your fattest come out and fight!”

sentences.zh: 」梁驍將鄧季筠引軍出戰，存孝舞槊擒之，李讜敗走，追擊至馬牢關。

translations.literal: Liang’s fierce general Deng Jiyun led troops out; Cunxiao danced his spear and seized him; Li Chan was beaten and fled; pursuit reached Malao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Liang’s champion Deng Jiyun sallied forth; Cunxiao whirled his spear and took him alive; Li Chan broke and ran; the chase ran to Malao Pass.

sentences.zh: 還攻潞州，唐以孫揆為潞州節度使，揆儒者，以梁卒三千為衛，褒衣大蓋，擁節先驅。

translations.literal: He returned to attack Lu Prefecture; Tang made Sun Kui military governor of Lu; Kui was a Confucian scholar, took three thousand Liang troops as guard, wore loose robes and a great canopy, and bore the commission at the van.
translations.idiomatic: He turned back on Luzhou; the court named Sun Kui its governor—a scholar who marched with three thousand Liang guards in flowing robes under a great canopy, the commission borne ahead.

sentences.zh: 存孝以三百騎伏長子西崖谷間，伺揆軍過，橫擊斷之，擒揆以歸。

translations.literal: Cunxiao hid three hundred horse in the western cliff valley at Changzi, waited for Kui’s column to pass, struck across and cut it off, seized Kui, and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao laid three hundred riders in the western cliff pass at Changzi, ambushed Kui’s march, cut the column in two, and carried Kui off.

sentences.zh: 初，梁遣葛從周、朱崇節守潞州以待揆，聞揆見執，皆棄去，晉遂復取潞州。

translations.literal: Earlier Liang had sent Ge Congzhou and Zhu Chongjie to hold Lu Prefecture awaiting Kui; hearing Kui was taken, both abandoned the city and fled, and Jin recovered Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had posted Ge Congzhou and Zhu Chongjie at Luzhou to receive Kui; when they learned he was captured, both fled, and Jin took the city back.

sentences.zh: 是時，張浚、韓建伐晉，擊陰地關，晉以李存信、薛阿檀等當浚，別遣存孝軍於趙城。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Jun and Han Jian attacked Jin and struck Yindi Pass; Jin set Li Cunxin and Xue Atan against Jun and separately sent Cunxiao’s army to Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun and Han Jian were then marching on Jin and hit Yindi Pass; Jin met Jun with Cunxin and Xue Atan and sent Cunxiao to Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 唐軍戰敗於陰地關，浚退保晉州，韓建走絳州。

translations.literal: Tang troops were defeated at Yindi Pass; Jun withdrew to hold Jin Prefecture, and Han Jian fled to Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tang lost at Yindi; Jun fell back to Jinzhou, and Han Jian ran to Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 存孝攻晉州，浚兵出戰，輒復敗，因閉壁不敢出。

translations.literal: Cunxiao attacked Jin Prefecture; Jun’s troops came out and were beaten again; he then shut the walls and dared not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao pressed Jinzhou; Jun sallied and lost again, then barred the gates and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 存孝去，攻絳州。

translations.literal: Cunxiao left and attacked Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao withdrew and turned on Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 浚、建皆走。

translations.literal: Jun and Jian both fled.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Jian both ran.

sentences.zh: 存孝猨臂善射，身被重鎧，櫜弓坐槊，手舞鐵楇，出入陣中，以兩騎自從，戰酣易騎，上下如飛。

translations.literal: Cunxiao had ape-long arms and excelled at archery; he wore heavy armor, quivered his bow and rode with spear upright, whirled an iron mace in hand, moved through the battle lines, kept two mounts at his side, and when the fight grew hot changed horses mid-charge—up and down like flight.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao’s arms were long as an ape’s and his bow never missed; in heavy mail he rode with bow slung and spear braced, swinging an iron mace through the press, two spare horses at his heel—when the fight peaked he changed mounts in a flash, rising and dropping like a bird in flight.

sentences.zh: 初，存孝取潞州功為多，而太祖別以大將康君立為潞州留後，存孝為汾州刺史，存孝負其功，不食者數日。

translations.literal: Earlier, in retaking Lu Prefecture Cunxiao’s merit was greatest, yet Taizu separately made the great general Kang Junli acting governor of Lu while Cunxiao was made prefect of Fen; Cunxiao resented his merit and fasted for days.
translations.idiomatic: He had done most to retake Luzhou, yet Taizu gave the post to Kang Junli and made Cunxiao only prefect of Fen; bitter at the slight, he refused food for days.

sentences.zh: 及走張浚，遷邠州刺史。

translations.literal: After driving off Zhang Jun he was transferred to prefect of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Jun was routed he became prefect of Bin.

sentences.zh: 大順二年，徙邢州留後。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dashun he was moved to acting governor of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Dashun 2 (891) he was shifted to acting governor of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，晉軍連歲攻趙常山，存孝常為先鋒，下趙臨城、元氏。

translations.literal: At that time Jin armies attacked Zhao’s Changshan year after year; Cunxiao was often vanguard and took Lincheng and Yuan Clan for Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had hammered Zhao’s Changshan for years; Cunxiao usually led the van and seized Lincheng and Yuan Clan.

sentences.zh: 趙王求救於幽州李匡威，匡威兵至，晉軍輒引去。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhao begged aid from Li Kuangwei of Youzhou; when Kuangwei’s troops arrived, the Jin army always withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhao called on Li Kuangwei of Youzhou; whenever Kuangwei marched in, Jin pulled back.

sentences.zh: 存孝素與存信有隙，存信譖之曰：「存孝有二心，常避趙不擊。

translations.literal: Cunxiao had long been at odds with Cunxin; Cunxin slandered him, saying: “Cunxiao has two hearts and always avoids Zhao without striking.”
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao and Cunxin had long hated each other; Cunxin whispered: “Cunxiao is disloyal—he skirts Zhao and will not strike.”

sentences.zh: 」存孝不自安，乃附梁通趙，自歸於唐，因請會兵以代晉。

translations.literal: Cunxiao felt unsafe, attached himself to Liang to reach Zhao, submitted to Tang in his own person, and asked to join armies to replace Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Cunxiao turned to Liang to open a road into Zhao, came over to Tang himself, and asked for allied armies to overthrow Jin.

sentences.zh: 唐命趙王王镕援之。

translations.literal: Tang ordered the Prince of Zhao Wang Rong to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: Tang ordered the Prince of Zhao, Wang Rong, to his aid.

sentences.zh: 明年，趙與幽州有隙，懼而與晉和，反以兵三萬助晉擊存孝。

translations.literal: The next year Zhao quarreled with Youzhou, grew afraid, made peace with Jin, and in turn sent thirty thousand troops to help Jin strike Cunxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Zhao feuded with Youzhou, panicked, reconciled with Jin, and sent thirty thousand men to help Jin crush Cunxiao.

sentences.zh: 存孝嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Cunxiao shut the city and held it alone.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao barred the gates and defended alone.

sentences.zh: 太祖自將兵傅其城，掘塹以圍之，存孝出兵沖擊，塹不得成。

translations.literal: Taizu personally led troops to invest the walls, dug trenches to encircle him; Cunxiao sallied and struck, and the trenches could not be finished.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu came in person to press the siege and dig encircling trenches; Cunxiao charged out and the ditches never closed.

sentences.zh: 裨將袁奉韜使人說存孝曰：「公所畏者，晉王爾。

translations.literal: Staff officer Yuan Fengtao sent someone to persuade Cunxiao: “What you fear is only the Prince of Jin.”
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Yuan Fengtao sent word: “You fear only the Prince of Jin.”

sentences.zh: 王俟塹成，且留兵去，諸將非公敵也，雖塹何為？

translations.literal: Once the trenches are done he will leave troops and depart; the other generals are no match for you—what harm can trenches do?”
translations.idiomatic: “When the ditches are finished he will march away and leave others behind—none of them can stand to you. What is a trench to you?”

sentences.zh: 」存孝以為然，縱兵成塹。

translations.literal: Cunxiao thought it sound and let his troops allow the trenches to be completed.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao believed him and stood his men down while the encirclement was dug.

sentences.zh: 塹成，深溝高壘，不可近，存孝遂窘。

translations.literal: The trenches were finished—deep moats and high ramparts, impossible to approach—and Cunxiao was driven to straits.
translations.idiomatic: The ring closed—deep ditch, high wall, no way in—and Cunxiao was trapped.

sentences.zh: 城中食盡，登城呼曰：「兒蒙王恩，位至將相，豈欲舍父子而附仇讎，乃存信構陷之耳。

translations.literal: Food in the city ran out; he mounted the wall and called: “Your son received the Prince’s grace and rose to general and minister—would I abandon father and son to cling to an enemy? It was Cunxin who framed me.”
translations.idiomatic: When the stores were gone he climbed the wall and cried: “I owed the Prince everything, rose to general and minister—would I trade father and son for a foe? Cunxin set this trap.”

sentences.zh: 願生見王一言而死。

translations.literal: I wish only to see the Prince alive once and then die.”
translations.idiomatic: Let me see the Prince once while I live, then die.”

sentences.zh: 」太祖哀之，遣劉夫人入城慰諭之。

translations.literal: Taizu pitied him and sent Lady Liu into the city to comfort and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was moved and sent Lady Liu into the city to reason with him.

sentences.zh: 劉夫人引與俱來，存孝泥首請罪曰：「兒於晉有功而無過，所以至此，由存信為之耳！

translations.literal: Lady Liu led him out together; Cunxiao pressed his face in the dust and begged forgiveness: “Your son served Jin with merit and without fault—what brought me here was Cunxin’s doing!”
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu brought him out; Cunxiao groveled and pleaded: “I served Jin with merit and no crime—Cunxin alone drove me to this!”

sentences.zh: 」太祖叱曰：「爾為書檄，罪我百端，亦存信為之邪？

translations.literal: Taizu shouted: “You wrote letters and proclamations heaping blame on me in a hundred ways—was that also Cunxin’s doing?”
translations.idiomatic: Taizu roared: “You drafted letters blaming me on every count—was Cunxin writing those too?”

sentences.zh: 」縛載後車，至太原，車裂之以徇。

translations.literal: He was bound and loaded on a rear cart, taken to Taiyuan, and dismembered by chariots as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: They bound him on a baggage cart, hauled him to Taiyuan, and tore him apart between chariots for all to see.

sentences.zh: 然太祖惜其材，悵然恨諸將之不能容也，為之不視事者十餘日。

translations.literal: Yet Taizu regretted his talent, sighed that his generals could not tolerate him, and for more than ten days would not attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu still mourned his gifts, cursed his generals for their jealousy, and for ten days would not hold court.

sentences.zh: 康君立素與存信相善，方二人之交惡也，君立每左右存信以傾之。

translations.literal: Kang Junli had always been friendly with Cunxin; while the two were at enmity, Junli always sided with Cunxin to bring Cunxiao down.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Junli favored Cunxin; while the feud burned, Junli always backed Cunxin to topple Cunxiao.

sentences.zh: 存孝已死，太祖與諸將博，語及存孝，流涕不已，君立以為不然，太祖怒，鴆殺君立。

translations.literal: After Cunxiao was dead, Taizu was gaming with his generals; when talk turned to Cunxiao he wept without end; Junli thought this wrong; Taizu was enraged and poisoned Junli.
translations.idiomatic: After Cunxiao’s death Taizu gambled with his commanders; mention of Cunxiao brought endless tears; Junli scoffed; Taizu in rage gave him poison.

sentences.zh: 君立初為雲州牙將，唐僖宗時，逐段文楚，與太祖俱起雲中，蓋君立首事。

translations.literal: Junli had first been a Yun Prefecture guard officer; in Emperor Xizong’s time he drove out Duan Wenchu and rose with Taizu from Yunzhong—Junli was the first to take up the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Junli began as a guard officer at Yunzhou; under Xizong he expelled Duan Wenchu and rose with Taizu from Yunzhong—the first man in the enterprise.

sentences.zh: 其後累立戰功，表昭義節度使，以存孝故殺之。

translations.literal: Later he piled up battle honors, was recommended military governor of Zhaoyi, and was killed on Cunxiao’s account.
translations.idiomatic: He won battle after battle, was named governor of Zhaoyi, and died for Cunxiao’s sake.

sentences.zh: 存進，振武人也，本姓孫，名重進。

translations.literal: Cunjin was a man of Zhenwu; originally surnamed Sun, personal name Chongjin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunjin came from Zhenwu; born Sun Chongjin.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻破朔州得之，賜以姓名，養為子。

translations.literal: When Taizu stormed Shuozhou and took him, he was granted the surname and personal name and raised as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu seized him when Shuozhou fell, gave him the Li name, and adopted him.

sentences.zh: 從太祖入關破黃巢，以為義兒軍使。

translations.literal: He followed Taizu through the passes to break Huang Chao and was made commander of the Adopted Sons Army.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the passes with Taizu against Huang Chao and became commander of the Adopted Sons Army.

sentences.zh: 從莊宗戰柏鄉，遷行營馬步軍都虞候，歷慈、沁二州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed Zhuangzong at Bai Township, was promoted to chief adjutant of the campaign horse and foot, and served as prefect of Ci and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He fought with Zhuangzong at Bai Township, became chief adjutant of horse and foot in the field army, and governed Ci and Qin.

sentences.zh: 莊宗初得魏博，以為天雄軍都部署，治梁亂軍，一切以法，人有犯者，輒梟首磔屍於市，魏人屏息畏之。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong first took Weibo he made him overall commander of the Tianxiong Army, disciplined Liang’s mutinous troops, and applied the law to everything; whoever offended was beheaded and his corpse dismembered in the market—the people of Wei held their breath in fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong first held Weibo he named him commander of Tianxiong and ruled Liang’s mutineers by strict law—offenders lost their heads and were quartered in the market until Wei dared not breathe.

sentences.zh: 從戰河上，以功遷振武軍節度使。

translations.literal: He followed the battles on the river and by merit was made military governor of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: He fought along the Yellow River and rose to governor of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 是時，晉軍德勝，為南北寨，每以舟兵來往，頗以為勞，而河北無竹石，存進乃以葦笮維大艦為浮梁。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin army was at Desheng with north and south stockades, moving troops by boat back and forth—a great labor; north of the river there was no bamboo or stone, so Cunjin lashed great ships with reed bundles to make a floating bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then held Desheng in twin camps and ferried troops by boat—a weary business; with no bamboo or stone in Hebei, Cunjin bound great hulls with reed fascines into a floating bridge.

sentences.zh: 莊宗大喜，解衣以賜之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was greatly pleased and stripped off his own robe to bestow it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong rejoiced and gave him the coat off his back.

sentences.zh: 晉討張文禮於鎮州，久不克，而史建瑭、閻寶、李嗣昭相次戰歿，乃以存進代嗣昭為招討使，軍於東垣渡。

translations.literal: Jin campaigned against Zhang Wenli at Zhen Prefecture and could not take it for a long time; Shi Jiantang, Yan Bao, and Li Sizhao died in battle one after another; Cunjin was then made to replace Sizhao as overall commander and encamped at Dongyuan Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Jin besieged Zhang Wenli at Zhenzhou without success; Shi Jiantang, Yan Bao, and Li Sizhao fell in turn; Cunjin replaced Sizhao as commander and camped at Dongyuan Ford.

sentences.zh: 東垣土惡，築壘不能就，存進伐木為柵。

translations.literal: The soil at Dongyuan was bad and fortifications could not be raised; Cunjin felled trees to make palisades.
translations.idiomatic: Dongyuan’s ground was foul and walls would not stand; Cunjin cut timber for stockades.

sentences.zh: 晉軍晨出芻牧，文禮子處球以兵千餘逼存進柵，存進出戰橋上，殺處球兵殆盡，而存進亦歿於陣。

translations.literal: At dawn Jin troops went out for fodder; Wenli’s son Chuchiu pressed Cunjin’s palisade with more than a thousand men; Cunjin fought on the bridge, killed nearly all of Chuchiu’s force, and himself died in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Jin herded fodder; Wenli’s son Chuchiu hit the stockade with a thousand men; Cunjin met him on the bridge, wiped out nearly all his troops, and fell in the fight.

sentences.zh: 追贈太尉。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子漢韶，明宗時復本姓，為洋州節度使。

translations.literal: His son Han Shao, in Mingzong’s time, recovered his original surname and became military governor of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Han Shao, under Mingzong, took back the Sun surname and governed Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 潞王從珂以鳳翔反，漢韶與張虔釗會唐軍討之，唐軍皆降於從珂，獨漢韶與虔釗軍不降，俱奔於蜀。

translations.literal: When Prince of Lu Congke rebelled from Fengxiang, Han Shao and Zhang Qianzhao joined Tang armies to punish him; the Tang armies all surrendered to Congke—only Han Shao and Qianzhao’s forces would not yield and both fled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Lu Congke rose at Fengxiang, Han Shao and Zhang Qianzhao marched with Tang to crush him; every Tang army turned to Congke—only theirs held out, then both fled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 事蜀，歷永平、興元、武信節度使。

translations.literal: Serving Shu, he held in turn the governorships of Yongping, Xingyuan, and Wuxin.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu he governed Yongping, Xingyuan, and Wuxin in succession.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘，卒於蜀。

translations.literal: Past seventy, he died in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Past seventy, he died in Shu.

sentences.zh: 存璋，字德璜，初與康群立、恭誌勤等從太祖入關，破黃巢，累遷義兒軍使。

translations.literal: Cunzhang, style Defang, at first with Kang Junli, Gong Zhizhiqin, and others followed Taizu through the passes, broke Huang Chao, and by degrees rose to commander of the Adopted Sons Army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunzhang, styled Defang, entered the passes with Kang Junli, Gong Zhizhiqin, and others against Huang Chao and rose to command the Adopted Sons Army.

sentences.zh: 太祖病革，存璋與張承業等受顧命，立莊宗為晉王，晉王以存璋為河東馬步軍使。

translations.literal: When Taizu was gravely ill, Cunzhang with Zhang Chengye and others received his final charge, installed Zhuangzong as Prince of Jin, and the Prince made Cunzhang commander of Hedong horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizu’s deathbed Cunzhang and Zhang Chengye took his last command and raised Zhuangzong as Prince of Jin; the Prince made Cunzhang commander of Hedong horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 晉自先王時，嘗優假軍士，軍士多犯法逾禁，莊宗新立，尤患之，存璋一切繩之以法，境內為之清肅。

translations.literal: From the former prince’s time Jin had often been lenient with soldiers, and many broke the law beyond bounds; Zhuangzong had just ascended and especially feared this; Cunzhang applied the law without exception, and within the borders all was made clean and stern.
translations.idiomatic: Since the old prince’s day Jin had indulged the ranks until lawlessness ran wild; the new Prince of Jin feared it most; Cunzhang bound every offense to the statute until the realm went still.

sentences.zh: 從攻夾城，戰柏鄉，以功遷汾州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed the assault on Jia City and fought at Bai Township; by merit he was made prefect of Fen.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Jiacheng and Bai Township and won Fenzhou by merit.

sentences.zh: 莊宗與劉鄩戰於魏博，梁遣王檀來，乘虛襲太原，存璋以汾州兵入太原距守，以功遷大同軍防禦使，遂為節度使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong battled Liu Yun at Weibo, Liang sent Wang Tan, who seized the moment to raid Taiyuan; Cunzhang led Fen troops into Taiyuan to hold it; by merit he was made defender of Datong Army and then military governor.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhuangzong fought Liu Yun at Weibo, Liang sent Wang Tan to strike Taiyuan in its weakness; Cunzhang rushed Fen troops in to hold the city, won Datong defender, then full governor.

sentences.zh: 天祐十九年以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Tianyou he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 19 (922) he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 追贈太尉。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 存賢，許州人也，本姓王名賢。

translations.literal: Cunxian was a man of Xuzhou; originally surnamed Wang, personal name Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxian came from Xuzhou; born Wang Xian.

sentences.zh: 少為軍卒，善角牴，太祖擊黃巢於陳州，得之，賜以姓名，養為子。

translations.literal: In youth he was a soldier, skilled at wrestling; when Taizu struck Huang Chao at Chen Prefecture he was taken, granted the surname and personal name, and raised as a son.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a common soldier and excelled at wrestling; Taizu took him fighting Huang Chao at Chenzhou, gave him the Li name, and adopted him.

sentences.zh: 後為義兒軍副兵馬使，遷沁州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was deputy commander of the Adopted Sons Army horse and foot and was made prefect of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He became deputy commander of the Adopted Sons Army and governor of Qin.

sentences.zh: 先時，沁州當敵沖，徙其南百餘里，據險立柵而寓居。

translations.literal: Earlier Qin Prefecture lay on the enemy’s highway; its seat was moved more than a hundred li south, a stockade built on difficult ground, and the people lodged there in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Qin had once stood in the enemy’s path; the seat was shifted a hundred li south to a cliff-side stockade while the people lived in exile.

sentences.zh: 至存賢為刺史，曰：「徙城避敵，豈勇者所為？

translations.literal: When Cunxian became prefect he said: “Moving a city to flee the enemy—is that what the brave do?”
translations.idiomatic: As prefect Cunxian said: “Abandoning a city to dodge the foe—is that courage?”

sentences.zh: 」乃復城故州。

translations.literal: He then restored the old prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt the old seat.

sentences.zh: 梁兵屢攻之，存賢力自距守，卒不能近。

translations.literal: Liang troops attacked repeatedly; Cunxian strained to hold them off and in the end they could not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Liang struck again and again; Cunxian held hard until they could not come near.

sentences.zh: 遷武州刺史、山北團練使，又遷慈州。

translations.literal: He was moved to prefect of Wu and regent of the Shanbei circuit, then again to Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Wu and regent Shanbei, then was shifted to Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 天祐十八年，梁兵攻朱友謙於河中，莊宗遣存賢援友謙。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Tianyou Liang troops attacked Zhu Youqian at Hezhong; Zhuangzong sent Cunxian to relieve Youqian.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 18 (921) Liang besieged Zhu Youqian at Hezhong; Zhuangzong sent Cunxian to his aid.

sentences.zh: 是時，友謙新叛梁歸晉，而河中食少，人心多貳，諜者因謂存賢曰：「河中人欲殺子以歸梁，宜亟去。

translations.literal: At that time Youqian had just defected from Liang to Jin, yet Hezhong had little food and hearts were divided; a spy therefore told Cunxian: “The people of Hezhong mean to kill you and return to Liang—you should leave at once.”
translations.idiomatic: Youqian had only just left Liang for Jin; Hezhong was short of grain and loyalty wavered; a spy warned Cunxian: “They will kill you and go back to Liang—flee now.”

sentences.zh: 」存賢曰：「死王事，吾誌也。

translations.literal: Cunxian said: “To die in the prince’s service is my wish.”
translations.idiomatic: Cunxian said: “To die for the prince is what I want.”

sentences.zh: 復何恨哉！

translations.literal: What regret could there be!
translations.idiomatic: What is there to regret?

sentences.zh: 」卒擊走梁兵。

translations.literal: In the end he struck and drove off the Liang army.
translations.idiomatic: He fought until Liang broke and ran.
